name: rtk
tagline: Cut tool-call tokens, keep every failure line.
summary: A CLI that filters noisy command output down to what an agent or a human actually needs. Per-tool parsers collapse passing-test spam while preserving every critical line — and CI fails if a critical line is ever lost.

authorship.role: Sole author — parsers, compression strategies, benchmark harness.
built: Per-tool parsers for vitest, tsc, Next build and generic CI logs
Structural compression: JSON schema-aware collapsing, diff, stack and dedup passes
The benchmark harness and its committed evidence artifacts, plus the CI gate that fails on any lost critical line
notBuilt: The tokenizer used to report token counts and cost in the benchmark table

caseStudy.problem: An agent reading raw tool output pays for thousands of lines confirming that nothing went wrong. A 200-test vitest run is roughly sixty thousand characters, almost all of which says 'passed'. Naive truncation is worse than the disease: it drops the failure that was the reason for running the command in the first place.
caseStudy.approach: Treat every tool as its own parsing problem rather than compressing generic text. Each parser knows what a critical line looks like for that tool, so passing noise can be collapsed aggressively while failures survive intact. The guarantee is then made testable: a benchmark suite over deterministic fixtures measures both reduction and critical-line retention, and CI fails the build if retention ever drops.

architecture.summary: A parser registry in front of a structural compression stage, with preservation guarantees asserted by a committed benchmark rather than promised in the README.
architecture.invariant: Reduction is never allowed to trade against critical-line retention — CI fails if any critical line is lost.

tradeoffs.choice: Per-tool parsers instead of one general-purpose compressor
tradeoffs.gained: Reduction of 99% or better on the synthetic fixtures that dominate the benchmark. Captured real transcripts are still in single digits, so the figure has not yet been shown on production-shaped input.
tradeoffs.gaveUp: Every new tool needs its own parser. Unrecognised output falls back to generic structural compression and does noticeably less well.

tradeoffs.choice: Deterministic synthetic fixtures rather than recorded real-world logs
tradeoffs.gained: The benchmark is reproducible by anyone, runs in CI, and its numbers can be regenerated on demand.
tradeoffs.gaveUp: Fixtures are shaped like real output but are not real output, so the numbers describe representative cases rather than a measured production workload.

lessons: Publishing a reduction percentage without a retention percentage next to it would have made the tool look better and be less trustworthy. Pairing the two is what makes the number worth anything.
limitations: The benchmark corpus is internally curated tool output; no independent corpus exists.
LLM task-success was measured on narrow rtk-specific fixtures, not general agentic workflows.
Redaction covers common secret shapes by construction; novel formats pass through.

technical: Per-tool parsers for vitest, tsc and Next build, each defining what must never be dropped
Structural compression: JSON schema-aware collapsing, diff, stack and dedup passes for unhandled output
A benchmark harness over deterministic fixtures that measures reduction and critical-line retention together
A CI gate that fails the build if retention ever regresses — the guarantee is enforced, not promised
product: Cuts tool-call tokens for agents and humans without ever losing the failure line
Reports 0% reduction honestly when compression is not possible, rather than massaging the number
Pairs every reduction figure with a retention figure, which is what makes the number trustworthy

caseStudy.whyItMatters: This is the most technically legible proof of engineering here: an agent reading raw tool output pays for thousands of lines confirming that nothing went wrong, and this reduces that to something small without dropping the line the reader needed. The reduction strategies are published with their percentages and their failure modes, which is rare. It is also the honest counter-example on this site — its CI is currently red, the benchmark's 99% figure was measured on synthetic fixtures rather than captured production transcripts, and both are stated on the case study rather than smoothed over.
